candidates.title: News photo: Soo Line 2-8-2 No. 1003’s fall run
candidates.excerpt: HARTFORD, Wis. — The early-autumn weather was perfect on Saturday, Sept. 26, as Soo Line Mikado No. 1003 rambled across Wisconsin farmland between Hartford and Burnett, Wis. Temperatures in the low 70s drew hundreds out to watch the 113-year-old 2-8-2 cross country roads and pass classic Midwestern farm scenes. Here, the locomotive and train skirt a field outside the tiny village of Iron Ridge, Wis. The train is on its return leg, eastbound, returning to Hartford after turning and taking on coal in Burnette. The excursion took place on Watco’s Wisconsin & Southern Railroad. No. 1003 is a relatively large Mikado, weighing in at 250 tons and producing 53,947 pounds starting tractive effort. It was a member of the Soo Line’s L-1 class, operating across all parts of the railroad’s system. No. 1003 ran for 46 years before being retired in 1959. candidates.title: BNSF train derailed in Missouri by collision with dump truck
candidates.excerpt: JACKSON, Mo. — A locomotive and six cars of a BNSF train derailed on Sunday following a collision with a quarry dump truck in Cape Girardeau County. The Fruitland Area Fire Protection District said in a Facebook post that it was dispatched to a reported collision at 9:01 a.m., and arrived to find the driver of the truck required extraction from his vehicle. The driver, a 37-year-old Cape Girardeau man, was airlifted to a hospital in St. Louis for treatment of serious injuries, according to TV stations KFVS and WSIL. No injuries to the train crew were reported. The stations said the Missouri State Highway Patrol crash report says the incident occurred at a gate-protected crossing, with the train hitting the truck that was stationary on the tracks. No hazardous materials were involved. The accident location, about 20 miles north of Cape Girardeau, is on BNSF’s River Subdivision. — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire@firecrown.com. The two Wabtec FLXdrive locomotives are the first half of a four-unit order by Union Pacific (NYSE:UNP). The railroad said the remaining two battery-electric units are scheduled to arrive in October, completing a fleet that will operate in the greater Los Angeles area. The railroad said the tests will yield data on the units’ performance, reliability and operating capabilities. candidates.excerpt: A BNSF train carrying mixed freight caught fire during a burglary in Riverside, California, Thursday morning. The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago, BNSF told FreightWaves. Firefighters found an open upper container burning on the moving double-stack train. Officials have not identified the items inside or reported any stolen cargo. Riverside dispatchers received the first report at 4:40 a.m. near Chicago Avenue. Early information placed the train heading west from downtown. Crews later located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer. Crews move train for access Access problems prevented crews from reaching the flames at their first location. Incident commanders directed railroad personnel to reposition the equipment farther east.
